First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{12}}={[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{-12}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-12$ and $\phi =\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{12}} & =2{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{-12} \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-12\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-12\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-12\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-12\theta )]=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(12\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(12\theta )].
$$
